theory.intro: A **budget** is a plan comparing **income** (money received) and **expenses** (money spent) over a set time period. It helps manage spending, meet commitments, and build savings.
facts: All amounts must be converted to the **same time period** ($1\text{ year} = 52\text{ weeks} = 26\text{ fortnights} = 12\text{ months}$).

**Fixed expenses** are recurring costs with predictable amounts, such as rent, insurance, and loan repayments. A fixed amount does not necessarily make an expense essential: a recurring subscription can be fixed and discretionary.
**Discretionary expenses** are flexible, non-essential spending choices that can be reduced, such as dining out and entertainment.
The financial position is given by $\text{Budget Balance} = \text{Total Income} - \text{Total Expenses}$.
A **surplus** occurs when income exceeds expenses, while a **deficit** occurs when expenses exceed income.
An **emergency fund** is a savings reserve covering $3$ to $6$ months of essential living expenses.
steps: Convert all income and expense items to the same time period
Calculate total income and total expenses
Calculate the budget balance and determine if there is a surplus or deficit

workedExamples.question_text: Alex receives monthly take-home pay of $\$3200$ and spends $\$3450$ each month. Calculate the annual budget balance and state whether Alex is saving or dissaving.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Convert both amounts to annual values.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Annual income} &= \$3200\times12\\&=\$38\,400\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Annual expenses} &= \$3450\times12\\&=\$41\,400\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Budget balance} &= \text{Income}-\text{Expenses}\\&=\$38\,400-\$41\,400\\&=-\$3000\end{aligned}$
Alex has an annual deficit of $\$3000$ and is dissaving.

workedExamples.question_text: Priya receives take-home pay of $\$610$ per week. Her expenses are board of $\$180$ per week, transport of $\$45$ per week, entertainment of $\$110$ per fortnight, clothes of $\$210$ per month, and electricity of $\$240$ per quarter. Use $52$ weeks, $26$ fortnights, $12$ months and $4$ quarters per year. Prepare an annual budget and calculate her budget balance. State whether she is saving or dissaving.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Convert each item to an annual amount.
$\text{Annual income}=\$610\times52=\$31\,720$
$\text{Board}=\$180\times52=\$9360$
$\text{Transport}=\$45\times52=\$2340$
$\text{Entertainment}=\$110\times26=\$2860$
$\text{Clothes}=\$210\times12=\$2520$
$\text{Electricity}=\$240\times4=\$960$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total annual expenses}&=\$9360+\$2340+\$2860+\$2520+\$960\\&=\$18\,040\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Budget balance}&=\$31\,720-\$18\,040\\&=\$13\,680\end{aligned}$
Priya has an annual surplus of $\$13\,680$ and is saving.

workedExamples.question_text: Noah receives take-home pay of $\$500$ per week for $40$ term weeks and $\$800$ per week for $12$ holiday weeks. He also receives $\$1200$ annually from a second income source. Throughout the $52$-week year, his expenses are rent of $\$250$ per week, groceries of $\$100$ per week, transport of $\$60$ per fortnight, and other living expenses of $\$200$ per month. He also contributes $\$1800$ annually to an investment from his take-home income. Include this contribution in his budget outgoings. Calculate his annual budget balance and state whether he is saving or dissaving.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Calculate earnings for each part of the year, then add the second income.
$\text{Term earnings}=\$500\times40=\$20\,000$
$\text{Holiday earnings}=\$800\times12=\$9600$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total annual income}&=\$20\,000+\$9600+\$1200\\&=\$30\,800\end{aligned}$
Convert the regular expenses to annual values and include the investment contribution.
$\text{Rent}=\$250\times52=\$13\,000$
$\text{Groceries}=\$100\times52=\$5200$
$\text{Transport}=\$60\times26=\$1560$
$\text{Other living expenses}=\$200\times12=\$2400$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total annual outgoings}&=\$13\,000+\$5200+\$1560+\$2400+\$1800\\&=\$23\,960\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Budget balance}&=\$30\,800-\$23\,960\\&=\$6840\end{aligned}$
Noah has an annual surplus of $\$6840$ and is saving.

foundation.question_text: A worker receives weekly take-home pay of $\$560$ and spends $\$410$ each week. Calculate the annual budget balance and state whether the worker is saving or dissaving.
Liam receives fortnightly take-home pay of $\$1520$. His total fortnightly expenses are $\$1290$. Calculate his annual budget balance and state whether he is saving or dissaving.

Maya receives a net fortnightly income of $\$1400$.
Her fortnightly living expenses total $\$1180$.
Calculate Maya's annual budget balance and state whether she is in surplus (saving) or deficit (dissaving).
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Calculate total income and total expenses**
$\text{Annual income} = \$1400 \times 26 = \$36\,400$
$\text{Annual expenses} = \$1180 \times 26 = \$30\,680$
2. **Calculate the budget balance and determine if there is a surplus or deficit**
$\text{Budget balance} = \$36\,400 - \$30\,680$
$= \$5720\text{ surplus (saving)}$

development.question_text: An apprentice receives take-home pay of $\$680$ per week. His expenses are board of $\$190$ per week, transport of $\$50$ per week, a phone plan of $\$30$ per month, and entertainment of $\$100$ per fortnight. Calculate his annual budget balance and state whether he is saving or dissaving.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Annual income} = \$680 \times 52 = \$35\,360$
$\text{Board} = \$190 \times 52 = \$9880$
$\text{Transport} = \$50 \times 52 = \$2600$
$\text{Phone plan} = \$30 \times 12 = \$360$
$\text{Entertainment} = \$100 \times 26 = \$2600$
$\text{Total annual expenses} = \$9880 + \$2600 + \$360 + \$2600 = \$15\,440$
$\text{Budget balance} = \$35\,360 - \$15\,440$
$= \$19\,920\text{ surplus (saving)}$

development.question_text: Daniel receives take-home pay of $\$1700$ per fortnight. His expenses are rent of $\$300$ per week, groceries of $\$130$ per week, insurance of $\$110$ per month, and entertainment of $\$90$ per fortnight. Calculate his annual budget balance.

Jack earns $\$920$ per week. His regular expenses are: Rent $\$340$/week, Groceries $\$160$/week, Car insurance $\$130$/month, Electricity $\$390$/quarter ($4$ quarters/year), and Entertainment $\$150$/fortnight.
Calculate Jack's annual budget balance and determine his annual savings.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Annual income} = \$920 \times 52 = \$47\,840$
$\text{Rent} = \$340 \times 52 = \$17\,680$
$\text{Groceries} = \$160 \times 52 = \$8320$
$\text{Car insurance} = \$130 \times 12 = \$1560$
$\text{Electricity} = \$390 \times 4 = \$1560$
$\text{Entertainment} = \$150 \times 26 = \$3900$
$\text{Total annual expenses} = \$17\,680 + \$8320 + \$1560 + \$1560 + \$3900 = \$33\,020$
$\text{Annual balance} = \$47\,840 - \$33\,020$
$= \$14\,820\text{ savings}$

development.solution_text:

$\text{Groceries} = \$170 \times 52 = \$8840$
$\text{Transport} = \$160 \times 26 = \$4160$

mastery.question_text:
A dual-income household receives take-home pay of $\$1150$ per week and $\$2400$ per fortnight. Their annual fixed expenses total $\$48\,500$, and their discretionary expenses are $\$650$ per fortnight. In addition, they pay an annual retirement investment contribution of $\$12\,220$ from their take-home income. Include this contribution in their budget outgoings.
Calculate their net annual budget balance.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Income 1} = \$1150 \times 52 = \$59\,800$
$\text{Income 2} = \$2400 \times 26 = \$62\,400$
$\text{Total annual income} = \$59\,800 + \$62\,400 = \$122\,200$
$\text{Retirement investment} = \$12\,220$
$\text{Discretionary expenses} = \$650 \times 26 = \$16\,900$
$\text{Total annual expenses} = \$48\,500 + \$16\,900 + \$12\,220 = \$77\,620$
$\text{Net annual balance} = \$122\,200 - \$77\,620$
$= \$44\,580\text{ surplus}$

A university student receives take-home pay of $\$540$ per week during the $36$ academic term weeks and $\$920$ per week during the $16$ holiday weeks. Her expenses are rent of $\$280$ per week, groceries of $\$110$ per week, transport of $\$70$ per fortnight, and other living expenses of $\$260$ per month throughout the $52$-week year. Calculate her annual budget balance and state whether she is saving or dissaving.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Annual income} = (\$540 \times 36) + (\$920 \times 16) = \$19\,440 + \$14\,720 = \$34\,160$
$\text{Rent} = \$280 \times 52 = \$14\,560$
$\text{Groceries} = \$110 \times 52 = \$5720$
$\text{Transport} = \$70 \times 26 = \$1820$
$\text{Other living expenses} = \$260 \times 12 = \$3120$
$\text{Total annual expenses} = \$14\,560 + \$5720 + \$1820 + \$3120 = \$25\,220$
$\text{Budget balance} = \$34\,160 - \$25\,220$
$= \$8940\text{ surplus (saving)}$
